question: Show that the function $f(x)=2x+\sin x$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbb{R}$.
explanation:
Given function
$$f(x)=2x+\sin x$$
First derivative
Differentiating with respect to $x$,
$$f'(x)=2+\cos x$$
Range of the trigonometric term
For every real $x$,
$$-1\leq\cos x\leq1$$
Therefore,
$$f'(x)=2+\cos x\geq2-1=1$$
Sign of the derivative
Thus, $f'(x)>0$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$. A differentiable function whose derivative is positive throughout an interval is strictly increasing on that interval.
Conclusion
Hence, $f(x)=2x+\sin x$ is strictly increasing on $(-\infty,\infty)$.

options.A: Strictly decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$ because $f'(x)<0$ for all $x$
options.B: Strictly increasing on $\mathbb{R}$ because $f'(x)=2+\cos x>0$ for all $x$
